items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Now Howard Dedunne, Ed Thigpen, I guess that was during the Korean War, they were at Ft. Ord, they used to come up and sit in with us on Sundays.

ctx.x: But was it the same band?

Same band. When Lunceford’s band came through, white night, colored night. Basie’s band came through, white night, colored night. Glenn Miller band came through, white night, colored night. Louis came through with a group, colored night, white night. Fats Waller, colored night and a white night. But then when the war came, suddenly the population increased and people were working 24 hours a day in three 8-hour shifts. So people had plenty of money and they could go out and they didn’t mind, see, if you had to…
